case-sara.text: [Softly] After dinner I notice the apartment is quiet, and I start checking my phone again.
case-sara.suggestion: The quiet settles around you after dinner, and the phone becomes the one small place where he might still appear.

case-sara.text: [Numb] I tell people I'm fine, but I feel flat when I say it.
case-sara.suggestion: Fine comes out smooth, while something underneath has gone pale and still.

case-sara.text: [Sad] I found his jacket in the closet and stood there longer than made sense.
case-sara.suggestion: That jacket stops you in the doorway, a small piece of him pulling the whole loss back into the room.

case-sara.text: [Softly] Some mornings I forget for a second, and then I remember we are not together.
case-sara.suggestion: There is that one clear second, then the breakup drops back onto you like weight returning to the bed.

case-sara.text: [Embarrassed] When friends ask how I am, I give a short answer and change the subject.
case-sara.suggestion: The short answer closes the door quickly, while the real answer waits tight in your throat.

case-sara.text: [Sad] I stay on my phone late because going to sleep feels hard now.
case-sara.suggestion: It is as if the little light of the phone keeps you company when the night feels hard to face.

case-sara.text: [Softly] A song came on in a store, and I had to leave before I cried.
case-sara.suggestion: The first notes find you in the aisle, and suddenly grief is right there under the fluorescent lights.

case-sara.text: [Embarrassed] I keep thinking maybe I did something wrong, but I can't pin down what.
case-sara.suggestion: The mind keeps searching for the flaw, like if it can find the loose thread, the whole leaving might make sense.

case-sara.text: [Sad] Some nights I sit on the floor beside the bed for a while instead of getting in.
case-sara.suggestion: The floor becomes the place you fold into when the bed feels too exposed and wide.

case-sara.text: [Softly] When you are kind to me, I feel awkward and look away.
case-sara.suggestion: Kindness comes close, and it is almost too warm to take in, so your eyes drop to safer ground.

case-sara.text: [Matter-of-fact] I took his name off the mailbox. It needed doing. Coming home afterwards was harder than I expected.
case-sara.suggestion: As if that small change at the door made the absence inside feel much larger.

case-sara.text: [Controlled] I keep the evenings busy. When there's nothing planned, I notice how much I miss having someone to tell the little things to.
case-sara.suggestion: All the activity goes quiet, and there's that empty place where the day's little stories used to go.

case-michael.text: [Firm] When someone corrects me in front of the team, I get hot and stop listening.
case-michael.suggestion: It sounds like the heat rises as though a spotlight has suddenly swung onto you in front of everyone.

case-michael.text: [Tense] I go into meetings expecting people to mess up, and I hate that I do that.
case-michael.suggestion: You arrive already braced, like part of you is standing guard at the door before anyone speaks.

case-michael.text: [Tense] By the end of the day I realize how many comments I did not say.
case-michael.suggestion: It is as if the whole day is clenched shut, every sharp sentence still held behind your teeth.

case-michael.text: [Embarrassed] After I snap, I feel embarrassed, but I mostly try not to think about it.
case-michael.suggestion: The embarrassment sits there afterward, heavy and damp, while you try to step around it.

case-michael.text: [Defensive] When my wife sighs while I am explaining something, I assume she has already decided I am wrong.
case-michael.suggestion: That small sigh can cross the room like a charge, and your system braces before she has even spoken.

case-michael.text: [Tense] If someone says calm down during an argument, I get angrier immediately and stop hearing the rest.
case-michael.suggestion: It is as if those two words strike a match, and the anger flares before you can hear anything else.

case-michael.text: [Embarrassed] When I don't know the answer in a meeting, I feel exposed in front of everyone.
case-michael.suggestion: Not knowing opens a bare place, like all the competence you rely on has lost its cover for a second.

case-michael.text: [Defensive] I slam doors sometimes because I don't know what else to do with the feeling.
case-michael.suggestion: The door takes the feeling for you, loud enough to cover the smaller sting underneath.

case-michael.text: [Ashamed] After a fight, thinking about apologizing first makes me feel weak and smaller than her.
case-michael.suggestion: The apology feels like stepping onto lower ground, with everyone suddenly taller around you.

case-michael.text: [Ashamed] At night I replay the argument and hear how sharp I sounded.
case-michael.suggestion: The house goes quiet, but your own voice keeps echoing in the kitchen, still cutting after the fight is over.

case-michael.text: [Clipped] One small correction in a good report. I heard nothing else they said. That's irritating.
case-michael.suggestion: That one correction takes up the whole room, and the good work shrinks out of sight.

case-michael.text: [Controlled] I know my son is just asking for help. Still, when I can't answer straight away, I feel as if I've failed him.
case-michael.suggestion: Even a small question seems to put you under a spotlight where you have to know the answer immediately.

case-jason.text: [Quietly] When it's my turn in a meeting, I lose track of what I was going to say.
case-jason.suggestion: It is as if every face turns toward you and the sentence you had ready vanishes into thin air.

case-jason.text: [Hesitant] In meetings I keep my hands under the table because I worry people will notice me.
case-jason.suggestion: Even your hands have to stay hidden, as if one small sign could give you away.

case-jason.text: [Anxious] I practice what to say, but when people look at me, I freeze.
case-jason.suggestion: All the practiced words line up, then the eyes land on you and everything locks behind a sheet of ice.

case-jason.text: [Quietly] If people laugh nearby after I have spoken, I assume I did something strange.
case-jason.suggestion: The laugh travels across the room and points itself at you, even before you know what it was about.

case-jason.text: [Hesitant] When attention turns to me, I get quieter and try not to move much.
case-jason.suggestion: Your whole body starts shrinking in the chair, trying to stay present without being seen.

case-jason.text: [Anxious] When someone compliments me after a meeting, I smile, but I don't really believe it.
case-jason.suggestion: It is as if the compliment stops at the door. You hear it, but it does not quite get in.

case-jason.text: [Quietly] Sunday night I start feeling low when the apartment gets quiet, but I mostly just scroll.
case-jason.suggestion: The week arrives early in the room, and scrolling becomes a small moving light against the heaviness.

case-jason.text: [Quiet and ashamed] I rewrite simple messages over and over, then sometimes don't send them.
case-jason.suggestion: One small message becomes a narrow doorway, and every rewrite is another step back from being seen.

case-jason.text: [Anxious] Even saying hello in the hallway can sound wrong to me afterward.
case-jason.suggestion: That tiny hello keeps ringing in your ears, as if one ordinary word has become evidence against you.

case-jason.text: [Quietly] In groups, I keep track of where the exit is before I join the conversation.
case-jason.suggestion: The exit becomes the safest part of the room, the place your eyes hold onto when attention feels too close.

case-jason.text: [Flat] Everyone in the group chat seemed to know what to say. I wrote a reply, looked at it, and didn't send it.
case-jason.suggestion: The conversation keeps moving, and you're waiting at its edge with words you can't quite let out.

case-jason.text: [Matter-of-fact] I replayed the greeting all evening. It lasted about five seconds. It's annoying that I can't leave it alone.
case-jason.suggestion: Those five seconds keep circling back, like a tiny clip you can't stop playing.

case-laura.text: [Flat and guarded] Most mornings I get up, make coffee, answer the messages I have to answer, and notice I still do not feel much.
case-laura.suggestion: It sounds like the day is running in grey: everything keeps moving, but very little reaches you.

case-laura.text: [Distant] If a door slams at work, I know it is just a door, but for a minute I cannot keep track of what people are saying.
case-laura.suggestion: The sound gets there before reason does, an old alarm taking over the room while the conversation moves away from you.

case-laura.text: [Betrayed] I found out he had been seeing someone else, and now when he is kind I mostly think, don't be stupid again.
case-laura.suggestion: His kindness reaches a place that has already pulled the shutters closed, trying not to be fooled twice.

case-laura.text: [Ashamed] My daughter sent pictures from a trip and I could see it was lovely, but I mostly felt blank and then guilty for that.
case-laura.suggestion: The picture shows life and closeness, and inside it is like a window you can look through without being able to step into it.

case-laura.text: [Distant] Wine helps me turn things off at night. I pour it before I have decided what I am trying not to think about.
case-laura.suggestion: The glass becomes the dimmer switch, lowering the room inside you before anything sharp can fully arrive.

case-laura.text: [Slow and flat] I lie awake listening for sounds in the hallway, and I tell myself there is nothing to listen for.
case-laura.suggestion: It is as though you lie down, but something in you stays on watch, listening for the next sound.

case-laura.text: [Tense and tearful] Sometimes a song comes on and my eyes fill up, so I change it before I can really tell what it is about.
case-laura.suggestion: The music opens a small crack in the numbness, and you turn away before the feeling has room to come through.

case-laura.text: [Hopeless] When my ex starts explaining why he left, I stop trying to answer and just wait for it to be over.
case-laura.suggestion: Under his explanations, you fold inward and go quiet, the fight draining out until answering feels useless.

case-laura.text: [Tense and guarded] When someone says something kind to me, I usually correct it in my head or wait for the catch.
case-laura.suggestion: The kindness touches a locked door, and behind it something tightens before the words can be received.

case-laura.text: [Flat and guarded] I keep a bag packed by the door. I know it sounds dramatic, but I sleep better knowing it is there.
case-laura.suggestion: The bag sits there as a quiet exit, helping the part of you that never fully trusts the house to stay settled.

case-laura.text: [Flat] I packed his last things. Afterwards the flat was tidy, and I didn't know what to do with myself.
case-laura.suggestion: Everything is in its place now, but you are left standing in a space that doesn't yet feel like yours.

case-laura.text: [Guarded] My friend was kind. I said thank you. I didn't really let it affect me until she'd gone.
case-laura.suggestion: Perhaps the kindness only reaches you once the door is closed and you no longer have to guard the opening.

case-carlos.text: [Defensive] When someone smirks at me on the crew, I get tense fast and spend the next hour making sure nobody thinks I let it slide.
case-carlos.suggestion: That smirk seems to hit like a spark, and suddenly the next hour is spent making sure everyone knows you will not be pushed around.

case-carlos.text: [Macho] My father used to say only weak men talk about feelings, and I still hear that when people ask what is going on with me.
case-carlos.suggestion: His voice still stands in the room like a command, keeping the softer places locked up before anyone can see them.

case-carlos.text: [Tense and angry] I pace around the kitchen after fights because if I sit still, I start thinking about what she said and get more worked up.
case-carlos.suggestion: You wear a track into the kitchen floor, trying to push the charge down through your feet before it bursts out.

case-carlos.text: [Ashamed] I keep remembering the look on my son's face after I yelled, but then I tell myself every father loses it sometimes.
case-carlos.suggestion: His face stays there under the excuses, a small bruise of shame you keep trying to cover with reasons.

case-carlos.text: [Defensive] When my wife says I drink too much, I start listing everything I do for this family so she will drop it.
case-carlos.suggestion: Her words land like an accusation, and the list of what you provide becomes armor against feeling judged.

case-carlos.text: [Ashamed] After I blow up, everyone gets quiet, and I usually make some comment so we can move on.
case-carlos.suggestion: After the outburst, it is as if everyone holds their breath, and your comment rushes into that silence.

case-carlos.text: [Angry, tightly controlled] I get so angry that I stop talking, because if I keep going I do not trust what I will say.
case-carlos.suggestion: The words are clamped behind your teeth, all that heat held in because one more sentence could break loose.

case-carlos.text: [Worthless] If I back down in front of my son, I feel like I have taught him not to respect me.
case-carlos.suggestion: Backing down feels like shrinking in his eyes, as if your outline as a father fades right there in front of him.

case-carlos.text: [Tense and angry] In the car after a fight, I grip the wheel and tell myself not to react until I get home.
case-carlos.suggestion: Your hands become the brakes on the whole reaction, holding the heat in place until the drive is over.

case-carlos.text: [Worried] I worry my son is learning to check my mood before he decides whether it is safe to talk.
case-carlos.suggestion: That worry hits hard, the thought that your anger could become the weather he checks before stepping close.

case-carlos.text: [Clipped] He made the comment in front of the crew. I finished the job. I was still thinking about it at home.
case-carlos.suggestion: You carried on working, but that public sting kept travelling with you long after the shift ended.

case-carlos.text: [Controlled] My daughter watches before she speaks to me. I notice it. I don't like what that says about things at home.
case-carlos.suggestion: There's a pause between you now, as if she has to test the ground before taking a step towards you.

case-nina.text: [Tired] The second I sit down, I remember three things I have not done and get back up.
case-nina.suggestion: It is as if you have barely settled into the chair before a bell rings inside: there is more to do.

case-nina.text: [Hurt] Sometimes I feel used, and then I immediately think of all the reasons I should be more grateful.
case-nina.suggestion: The hurt rises for a second, and then gratitude is pulled over it like a blanket before anyone can see.

case-nina.text: [Worthless] When I need help, I feel embarrassed, like I have failed at the basic things everyone else handles.
case-nina.suggestion: Needing help makes you shrink, as if one request could lower your whole worth in the room.

case-nina.text: [Tired] I smile and keep going because if I stop, people ask if something is wrong and then I have to manage that too.
case-nina.suggestion: The smile becomes another job, stretched across the tiredness so no one has to look too closely.

case-nina.text: [Apologetic] By evening I am so tired I can barely answer my son, and then I apologize because he did not ask for a tired mother.
case-nina.suggestion: The tiredness is heavy in your voice, and even that becomes something you feel you have to make up for.

case-nina.text: [Torn] Saying no makes me panic, even about small things, because I start picturing the other person deciding I am selfish.
case-nina.suggestion: It is as if that small no could pull a thread loose between you, and suddenly the whole connection feels at risk.

case-nina.text: [Tired] I clean late at night even when I am exhausted, because waking up to a messy kitchen ruins the whole morning.
case-nina.suggestion: The counter gets wiped again, a midnight attempt to make tomorrow safe before you are allowed to stop.

case-nina.text: [Guilty] If the house is messy, I feel ashamed before anyone says anything, and I start explaining what got in the way.
case-nina.suggestion: Shame arrives before any criticism, and the explanations stack up in front of you like a shield.

case-nina.text: [Tearful] I cry in the kitchen where no one will notice, then splash my face and go back out.
case-nina.suggestion: The tears get hidden among ordinary kitchen sounds, washed away quickly so the household does not have to pause.

case-nina.text: [Lonely] I still wait for my ex to notice how tired I am, even though he does not live here anymore and probably never noticed.
case-nina.suggestion: Some part of you is still watching for him to look up, waiting for the old life to finally see how much you carried.

case-nina.text: [Matter-of-fact] I spent the afternoon finding things everyone else wanted. When they asked what I wanted, I couldn't think of anything.
case-nina.suggestion: You've made so much room for everyone else's wishes that your own seem tucked away where you can barely reach them.

case-nina.text: [Smiling, detached] They said I always keep things going. It was meant as a compliment. I felt tired hearing it.
case-nina.suggestion: The compliment lands almost like another load placed in the arms already carrying everything.

case-aisha.text: [Distrustful] You say your notes are private, but if you write that I am unstable, I will not know until it is already out there.
case-aisha.suggestion: It is as if the words on that page could travel somewhere you cannot follow, leaving you with no say in how you are seen.

case-aisha.text: [Desperate] I can beg someone to stay and then tell them to leave me alone in the same conversation, and I mean both at the time.
case-aisha.suggestion: The feeling swings from reaching for their sleeve to shoving the door closed, both moves trying to survive the same fear.

case-aisha.text: [Confused] I cannot tell if I am angry, scared, or empty; by the time I choose one word, it has already changed.
case-aisha.suggestion: It is all tangled and moving at once, like trying to open one door while the hallway keeps rearranging around you.

case-aisha.text: [Panicked] I scratch my arm when I start feeling unreal, because looking around the room and naming objects does not always bring me back.
case-aisha.suggestion: The scratching becomes an urgent way to feel real again, a sharp signal when the room starts drifting away.

case-aisha.text: [Panicked] When the typing dots disappear, I check the message again and again, even if I know they probably just got busy.
case-aisha.suggestion: Those vanishing dots pull the thread of contact out of your hands, and suddenly the whole connection feels suspended.

case-aisha.text: [Desperate] When someone says goodbye, I know it is normal, but I start bargaining in my head about how to keep them there longer.
case-aisha.suggestion: It sounds like goodbye starts closing a door, and you are already reaching to hold it open a little longer.

case-aisha.text: [In denial] Last week I felt suicidal when he disappeared, but then he texted me back, so maybe I am fine now and we do not need to make it a big thing.
case-aisha.suggestion: His message may have felt like a lifeline after that frightening week. I do not want to assume the suicidal thoughts are gone because he replied. Are you having thoughts of ending your life now?

case-aisha.text: [Hurt] When someone calls me too much, I keep hearing it afterward, especially when I want to text them and try not to.
case-aisha.suggestion: Too much lands like a stamp across you, bright and hard to wash off, exactly where the wish for contact lives.

case-aisha.text: [Tearful] When someone is gentle with me, I cry before I understand why, and then I get embarrassed and want them to stop being nice.
case-aisha.suggestion: Gentleness gets through before you can brace, tears rush up, and then shame tries to push the kindness back out.

case-aisha.text: [Panicked] I keep checking the door while we talk, because part of me expects you to stand up and leave if I say too much.
case-aisha.suggestion: Your eyes keep guarding the doorway, watching for the moment I might vanish because the need became too visible.

case-aisha.text: [Flat, deliberate] I delete the conversation so I won't check it. Then I open the empty screen. I do that too.
case-aisha.suggestion: Even when the messages are gone, it's as though you're still waiting at the same door for someone to come back.

case-aisha.text: [Guarded] Things are fine today. I don't want to get used to it. That's usually when something changes.
case-aisha.suggestion: You can feel the calm nearby, but you keep one hand on the alarm in case it disappears.

case-david.text: [Controlled] When my wife calls me cold, I get quiet and then make one precise comment that I know will land hard.
case-david.suggestion: It sounds as though "cold" lands like a blow, and your words strike back.

case-david.text: [Worthless] If I am not the best person in the room, I feel ordinary, and ordinary is almost worse than failing.
case-david.suggestion: The floor opens under ordinary, and you drop from impressive to nothing before anyone else has even judged you.

case-david.text: [Defensive] When I feel small, I start talking about what I have achieved, even if the conversation had nothing to do with work.
case-david.suggestion: The achievements rush in like a taller version of you, surrounding the small, stung place before it can be seen.

case-david.text: [Controlled] When I feel cornered, I fix my shirt, slow my voice, and start explaining my record so the room remembers who I am.
case-david.suggestion: The shirt, the voice, and the record become armor pieces fastened one by one before the hit can land.

case-david.text: [Ashamed] No matter how much I achieve, I still think there is something wrong with me, and I hate that success has not fixed it.
case-david.suggestion: Each success adds another polished layer, while underneath there is a stain you fear achievement can never cover.

case-david.text: [Ashamed] My kid's face after I snap bothers me more than I expected, but I still catch myself preparing a defense.
case-david.suggestion: It is as if your child's face stays there between you and every argument you reach for.

case-david.text: [Avoidant] In hard talks, I check my phone when it gets too personal, and I tell myself I am just staying on top of things.
case-david.suggestion: The phone becomes a trapdoor under the table, a clean exit before the feeling can corner you.

case-david.text: [Dismissive] Saying I was wrong feels humiliating, even when part of me knows I caused the damage.
case-david.suggestion: Those words strip the armor in an instant, leaving your face hot and exposed in front of the damage.

case-david.text: [Confused] I do not know what I feel; I just know I cannot settle when everyone goes quiet after I have spoken.
case-david.suggestion: The quiet turns into a hallway of closed doors, and you pace there without knowing which one holds the feeling.

case-david.text: [Controlled] Since the affair came out, home feels different; people still use the same rooms, but I do not know where I stand.
case-david.suggestion: The house still has the same rooms, but the warmth has leaked out, leaving you standing without a clear place.

case-david.text: [Coolly] The dinner was a success. Everyone praised the house. Once they left, it felt remarkably empty. That's not a complaint, just an observation.
case-david.suggestion: The applause leaves with the guests, and you're standing in the quiet it no longer fills.

case-david.text: [Controlled] I've rewritten the email several times. There is nothing wrong with it now. Sending it still seems to give them too much opportunity to judge me.
case-david.suggestion: You keep polishing the surface, but sending it still feels like stepping out without any cover.

case-marcus.text: [Hopeless] Most days I go through the motions, show up where I am supposed to, and still do not see the point of talking about it.
case-marcus.suggestion: It sounds like moving through a day with all the colour washed out, and talking feels like more effort with nowhere to go.

case-marcus.text: [Low voice] Crowds make me tense before anything has happened; I track exits, hands, and noise while everyone else is just shopping.
case-marcus.suggestion: The crowd reaches you as threat before it reaches you as people, and your whole system takes up its post.

case-marcus.text: [Macho] In the unit, feelings got people killed, so I learned not to have them, and I still do not know what good they are supposed to do.
case-marcus.suggestion: That rule still sounds like an order in your chest: feelings get people killed, so the heart gets locked behind a door.

case-marcus.text: [Hypervigilant] Nightmares wake me up, and then the room does not feel normal for a while; I check the corners even though I know where I am.
case-marcus.suggestion: Sleep throws you back into a charged room, as if danger followed you out and waited in the corners.

case-marcus.text: [Low voice] When the apartment is quiet, I feel worse, but I usually stay there because calling someone would be harder.
case-marcus.suggestion: The quiet presses in until even the air feels crowded, and staying alone becomes the familiar kind of endurance.

case-marcus.text: [Quiet and guarded] When something good happens, I notice it, say the right thing, and then wait for the feeling that does not come.
case-marcus.suggestion: It is as if something good is right in front of you, but there is a pane of glass between you and the feeling.

case-marcus.text: [Flat] I keep the lights low at home because bright light bothers me and makes the place feel too exposed.
case-marcus.suggestion: The dim light softens the edges, keeping the room from coming at you too clearly all at once.

case-marcus.text: [Low voice] If someone knocks unexpectedly, I get thrown off fast, even if it turns out to be a neighbor with the wrong apartment.
case-marcus.suggestion: The knock turns the door into danger for a moment, and your whole system starts hammering before a name appears.

case-marcus.text: [Confused] When I try to talk about it, I do not know what feeling is supposed to come first, so I usually stop talking.
case-marcus.suggestion: Every feeling crowds the same doorway, and none is clear enough to step through before the door closes again.

case-marcus.text: [Flat] Some nights I sit in the car before going upstairs, because once I open the apartment door there is nothing to do but be there.
case-marcus.suggestion: The quiet car becomes a last small shelter before the empty apartment has to be entered.

case-marcus.text: [Flat] I leave the television on. Not watching it. It's worse when the room is quiet.
case-marcus.suggestion: The sound seems to keep a little distance between you and what the silence brings close.

case-marcus.text: [Guarded] I recognised the handwriting on the envelope. Put it in a drawer. Haven't opened it. Don't want it in sight either.
case-marcus.suggestion: That familiar writing seems to bring something close enough that you need a drawer between you and it.
